title: When the Garden Turns
premise: Ansel Nakamura has spent a decade hiding in plain sight, selling harmless charms while guarding the sealed gate beneath their shop that leads to the court beneath the mountain. When a child named Iri arrives speaking the First Tongue and bearing a soul-token that matches one Ansel sold years ago under coercion, Ansel learns the court's magistrates have been buying souls to feed the last dragon-fire that sustains their power. To save Iri's stolen brother—and confront the part of themselves they buried when magic was outlawed—Ansel must cross the gate, outwit the court with the very charms they once called worthless, and choose between restoring the law's order or letting the old fire die. In the end, Ansel reopens the gate not as its keeper but as its breaker, freeing the souls and accepting exile as the price of justice the law will never grant.
about_author: Paloma Vasquez is a former botanist who left fieldwork to write fantasies rooted in gardens, borders, and the quiet violence of institutions. She lives in a coastal town where she keeps an illegal greenhouse of 'charmed' heirloom tomatoes.

chapters.title: The Shop That Sells Nothing
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. We meet Ansel tending their charm shop in the city of Vell, hiding the sealed gate beneath the floorboards and performing small, legal magics disguised as luck. A routine inspection by the Ministry of Order nearly exposes them. Emotional beat: the exhausting vigilance of a life built on invisibility.

chapters.title: A Child at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. On a rain-lashed night, Iri arrives barefoot, speaking the First Tongue—a language Ansel hasn't heard since before the outlawing—and clutches a soul-token etched with a name: her brother Tam. The token resonates with the gate below. Emotional beat: dread curdling into reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: What the Floorboards Remember
chapters.summary: Iri's POV. While Ansel sleeps, Iri senses the gate humming and glimpses memories stored in the house itself—Ansel's past as the gate's appointed keeper, and the night ten years ago when they let someone be taken rather than fight. Emotional beat: the child sees the adult's shame clearly.

chapters.title: The Debt of Charms
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel recognizes the soul-token's maker: Magistrate Corvane, who coerced Ansel years ago into crafting binding charms for the court. Confronting an old contact reveals the court beneath the mountain buys souls to feed the last dragon-fire, which sustains the magistrates' immortality. Emotional beat: guilt made concrete—Ansel's hands built the cage.

chapters.title: Ministry of Small Cruelties
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The Ministry raids the shop hunting Iri; Ansel triggers decades-old contingency charms to smuggle the child through the city's hidden ways. They shelter with a network of unlicensed hedge-witches who remember Ansel from before. Emotional beat: discovering that invisibility was never solitude—others kept the flame too.

chapters.title: Down the Stair That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel and Iri open the gate and descend into the court beneath the mountain, a cathedral of bone-white bureaucracy where souls are filed like debts. Ansel poses as a returning contractor while Iri's First Tongue unlocks doors no key fits. Emotional beat: terror sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: The Dragon-Fire Ledger
chapters.summary: Iri's POV. Deep in the archive, Iri finds the ledger of purchased souls—hundreds, including Tam's—and learns the fire is guttering because the court has overdrawn it. Corvane catches them but hesitates, revealing even he fears what happens when the fire dies. Emotional beat: the enemy is revealed as another captive.

chapters.title: Bargain at the Ember Throne
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Brought before the ember throne, Ansel is offered freedom and absolution if they renew the binding charms. Instead they offer a counter-bargain: their own keeper's oath, the oldest magic, to hold the fire without souls—if the court releases them all. The magistrates refuse; the fire flares to consume Ansel. Emotional beat: the temptation of easy redemption refused.

chapters.title: When the Garden Turns
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. Iri speaks the First Tongue to the fire itself, which remembers being alive, not fuel. The souls rise; the garden of ash above the court blooms green as the old magic turns against its jailers. Ansel breaks the gate from the inside, shattering the magistrates' immortality. Corvane, freed, opens the final door. Emotional beat: power returned to its source.

chapters.title: Keeper No Longer
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, epilogue. The court lies quiet, the dragon-fire free and small as a hearth-flame now tended by choice, not theft. Tam is restored to Iri; the hedge-witches begin rebuilding openly. Ansel, exiled by the surviving law but no longer hiding, plants a garden over the broken gate. Emotional beat: peace earned through loss—the end of invisibility as a beginning.
